Date: 6 February 2026
Time of call: 11:03am

I contacted my GP practice regarding an application my doctor and I have been following up on for the past three months. We finally received an update on 05.02.26, and I now have only six days to complete and return the required medical form.

During my call, the receptionist refused to pass the information to my doctor or provide an email address so I could forward the document, or arrange for someone to call me back. All I needed was a way to share the email so the doctor could review the form within the deadline.

I was also told to go through a private procedure route, even though this issue is unrelated to a private letter I previously paid for. This is a medical application form connected to my ongoing care, not a private service request.

I suffer from peripheral nerve disease and am currently undergoing treatment related to my head and neurological health. Delays and lack of cooperation in handling urgent medical matters are causing significant stress and are affecting my health and wellbeing. No other receptionist has caused this issue — staff have always previously been helpful and followed correct procedures.

GP practices have a duty of care under NHS regulations and the Health and Social Care Act 2008, as well as responsibilities set out in the NHS Constitution, to provide patients with fair access to care and not create barriers to medical support.
